title: The decision: what Approve and Send back do, and when
summary: A line above Approve says what it does in this exact state (the PR, its checks, landing, a run, the runner); four states ask first; a 5-second hold is the undo; what-if edits are counted apart, can be hidden, and are never dropped silently.

scenarios.title: A maintainer approves a draft spec PR with a check still running

steps.text: Opening the proposal reads its PR fresh: a draft, one check running, landing on approval on.
The line reads: PR #24 is a draft. Approve posts an approval; it lands only if the PR is marked ready within 60 minutes.
The first press asks in place: its author has not marked it ready. The maintainer presses Approve anyway.
Approving in 5 s, with Undo focused. Nothing has left the page; the facts are read once more at the end.
The approval is posted as the maintainer, and the spec.approved hook fires.
The lander waits for the PR to be ready and green; the decision foot shows Cancel landing.

scenarios.title: A maintainer approves while no runner is online, and is told the run will wait

steps.text: No runner token has polled for 2 hours.
The decision route says a code run follows an approval, and the runner is quiet.
The line ends: Then a code run is asked for. No runner has polled for 2 h: the run will wait.
Approve is allowed with one press: the approval does not depend on the runner.
The trigger asks for the run; it is queued until a runner polls.

scenarios.title: A maintainer sends a proposal back with an edit, and the agent folds it in

steps.text: The maintainer adds a node; it comes into view, marked once, and the counts read yours: +1 node.
My edits off shows the proposal as written, without undoing the edit.
Send back with a note: the line says it posts the note and 1 edit for the drafting agent, and asks for no run.
The comment is posted on the spec PR with the cornfield-review block; spec.sentBack carries the note and the edit.
The drafting agent reads the review with cornfield review.
applyEdits folds the edit into the proposal, and the agent pushes a new draft.
